title: Tenali Raman and the Syllogism of the Cat and the Curd

full_text:
A haughty scholar of Nyaya (formal logic) named Tarka Shastri arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, boasting that his mastery of syllogistic reasoning could prove anything in the universe, true or false.
Before King Krishnadevaraya, he argued:
'Maharaj, observe my flawless logical deduction:
Major Premise: All cats have four legs.
Minor Premise: My wooden dining table has four legs.
Conclusion: Therefore, my wooden dining table is an authentic living cat!
None can challenge the mathematical structure of formal logic!'

The courtiers looked baffled. While they knew the conclusion was absurd, none could untangle the philosophical sophistry.
King Krishnadevaraya was amused, but annoyed by the scholar's arrogance.

Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, Tarka Shastri’s logic is truly magnificent!
In fact, I have applied his exact philosophical syllogism to solve the palace dairy shortage!'

Tenali ordered a servant to bring a large clay bowl filled with rich, creamy white curd from the royal kitchens.
Tenali placed the bowl upon the scholar’s wooden table.
Tenali then turned to Tarka Shastri:
'Revered logician, since you have proven beyond dispute that your wooden dining table is an authentic living cat, let us observe its feline behavior!
Cats love nothing more than sweet milk and fresh curd.
Command your wooden table to lap up this bowl of curd!
If your table is a real cat, it will eat with pleasure. But if it fails to eat, your logic is nothing more than empty sophistry!'

The scholar stood frozen, staring at the motionless wooden table and the bowl of curd.
The court waited in silence.
One minute passed. Five minutes passed.
The wooden table, of course, did not move a single leg, nor did it lap up a drop of curd.

Tenali smiled with devastating wit:
'What is the matter, Master Logician? Is your table-cat feeling shy?
Or perhaps it prefers mice to curd?
A four-legged table remains dead timber, no matter how many clever words you spin to call it a cat!
When logic divorces itself from common sense and practical reality, it becomes the pastime of fools!'

King Krishnadevaraya and the entire court erupted in roaring laughter!
The haughty logician turned red with embarrassment, bowed his head, and conceded defeat.
The King awarded the bowl of sweet curd to Tenali Raman, celebrating that common sense is the master of all formal philosophy.
moral: Clever philosophical syllogisms that twist words to justify absurdities collapse when applied to practical life.
